extracted.intended_audience: Referees / peer reviewers invited to review manuscripts for Review Commons (journal-independent, preprint-focused peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting referee reports to Review Commons, including structure, tone, conflicts, anonymity, co-reviewing, and how to assess evidence, reproducibility, significance, and ethics. Intended to guide reviewers on what to evaluate and how to report it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain critical views (”review”) from independent experts; assess the validity of the study, its strengths, and weaknesses; provide constructive feedback to help authors improve their study; place the study in the context of the existing scientific knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the review as both quality control and a resource for readers and editors; focus on validity, strengths/weaknesses, constructive improvements, and contextualization within the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly tone and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons referee reports are expected to be scholarly in tone and content. Provide a clear, professional and impartial analysis that you would employ if you were signing the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of potential sources of bias with regard to the authors, including gender, ethnicity, geographical location, seniority, reputation. The Managing Editor may exclude reviews deemed unprofessional. Signing is encouraged but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely delivery is a hallmark of a good referee report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit reviews within agreed timelines to support efficient, journal-agnostic peer review and to help authors progress their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical and substantiated analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a critical and impartial analysis with substantiated arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back assertions with evidence or references; avoid unsupported opinions. Explain why you judge methods, data, or interpretations to be sufficient or deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and realistic suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer constructive and realistic suggestions to help authors improve their study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between essential requests and broader suggestions. Label far-reaching but nonessential improvements as “OPTIONAL”. Propose realistic changes and, where substantial, give estimated time/resource investment for suggested experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate and accurate referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Include adequate and accurate references to current knowledge and literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point authors to relevant prior work they may have missed and use references to substantiate claims about novelty or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewing transparency and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers (ECRs) may co-review provided the principal reviewer has carefully read the paper and mentors the process. The review form includes a field to list the names of all co-reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal reviewer must identify ECRs, ensure they are well-qualified, and take responsibility for the quality of the final review. Transparently list all co-reviewers on the review form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (structure of the report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short summary of the findings and key conclusions (including methodology and model system(s) where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the summary concise and factual; place comments about significance in the Significance section. The summary should orient editors/readers to the main claims and approaches used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major comments (structure of the report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address whether the claims and conclusions are supported by the data or require additional experiments/analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request additional experiments only if essential for the conclusions; otherwise ask authors to qualify claims as preliminary/speculative or remove them. If recommending experiments, indicate whether they are essential or OPTIONAL, assess whether they are realistic in time/resources, and provide estimated time when substantial. Evaluate reproducibility (are data and methods presented so they can be reproduced?), replication, and adequacy of statistical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor comments (structure of the report)
rubrics_metrics.description: List specific experimental issues that are easily addressable, referencing prior studies, and issues of presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include corrections or clarifications for text and figures, suggest improvements to presentation or clarity, and note missing or inappropriate citations that are straightforward to fix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contextual information about the novelty of the study, its value for the field, and the communities that might be interested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a general assessment of strengths and limitations, identify the strongest/most important aspects, and indicate what should be developed. Compare the study to the closest related results and describe the nature of the advance (conceptual, technical, clinical, mechanistic, functional, etc.). Describe the intended audience (specialized, broad, basic, translational/clinical) and how others might use the work. Define your field of expertise with a few keywords and indicate any parts you cannot evaluate due to lack of expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: No confidential comments to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons referee reports do not include ‘confidential comments to the editors’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are potential ethical breaches or data integrity issues, contact the editors directly (outside the public review form) rather than using a confidential-comments channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee cross-commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sending reviews back to authors, Review Commons will circulate the reports to all referees with an invitation to comment on each others’ reports where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in cross-commenting when invited. These referee-to-referee comments will be included in the full reports forwarded to the authors where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and disclosure to affiliate journals
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, referee identities are not communicated to authors unless a reviewer elects to sign their report. All referees must agree to disclose their names to any affiliate journals and to have their comments posted on a preprint server and/or as part of the transparent review process at an affiliated journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may sign their reports voluntarily. Some affiliate journals require sharing reviewer identities with other reviewers (but not authors); referees should agree in principle to participate in such consultative procedures. Review Commons will ask permission before forwarding reviewer names to a non-affiliate journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons will avoid inviting referees who have recent/ongoing collaborations with the authors, are engaged in similar research, have commented on drafts, are in direct competition, work in the same department/institution, have a personal relationship, have a history of dispute, or have a financial/personal interest in the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees must disclose anything that might affect their report and decline to referee if they cannot be objective. Prior review of another version elsewhere does not automatically exclude re-review unless the referee feels predisposed against the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should maintain strict confidentiality on all aspects of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts not yet publicly available as preprints should not be discussed with anyone not directly involved. If consulting external experts, check with the editors beforehand to avoid involving excluded parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity and ethical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees who are familiar with the field should alert the editors to potential breaches of publication policy or ethical conduct (e.g., plagiarism, author conflict of interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preferred, notify editors outside the formal peer-review form. Review Commons reserves the right to reject manuscripts at any point if ethical, biosecurity, or scientific integrity issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing revisions for affiliate journals
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a revised version for an affiliate journal, focus the evaluation on the points raised in the initial reviews and avoid raising new issues unless fatal flaws are discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact referees only when required for clarification or to evaluate data added in revision; do not request an editorial opinion on journal fit. If new issues arise from added data, request changes only if absolutely necessary and directly related to the major conclusions. If the manuscript is submitted to a non-affiliate journal, Review Commons will ask reviewers for permission before forwarding their names.
